structure: Part 3, live-animals journey pages. Read in full: src/k6/live-animals.js (the LIVE_ANIMALS_STEPS draft list of 12 steps, reEdit, amendEdit, planFor), src/k6/live-animals.test.js (2 tests), src/k6/journey-pages.js (save check, choice readers, page path, party picker with worst-case search, reachAndSubmit), src/k6/documents.js (accompanying-documents upload to cdp-uploader and scan-status poll), src/lib/form-fill.js and its test (blank-field fill rules, select options, species filter, d/m/yyyy date text), src/lib/forms.js and its test (hidden fields, prefilled fields, urlencoded body), src/lib/documents.js and its test (PDF and JPEG bytes, sizes, filenames, scan status settled and rejected), src/config/test-data.js (commodity search, worst-case search length, document issue date, scan poll and timeout, scan allowance, local stand-ins; its plants origins and potato arrival time belong to the plants journey, outside this source's scope) and the 'live-animals' entry of STEP_ENDPOINTS in src/config/journey-endpoints.js. Covered, in step order: origin, commodities (search then species), import-reason, consignment-details, commodities/identification, additional-details, accompanying-documents (upload and scan), addresses (5 party pickers), cph-number, port-of-entry, transit-countries (add then save), transporters; then reEdit, amendEdit and planFor, the endpoint tag names and the form-fill mechanics the steps rely on. Every path is relative to the notification base, which part 2 claims. The scripts read form names, option values and two radio labels; they read no headings, hints or error messages.

claims.statement: The performance walker fills a live-animals notification draft in 12 steps, in this order: origin, commodities, import-reason, consignment-details, identification, additional-details, documents, addresses, cph-number, port-of-entry, transit-countries, transporters.
claims.quote:
export const LIVE_ANIMALS_STEPS = Object.freeze({
  draft: [
    reachAndSubmit('origin', 'origin', ENDPOINTS.origin, originAnswers),
    commodities,
    reachAndSubmit(
      'import-reason', ... documentsStep,
    addresses,
    reachAndSubmit('cph-number', ... portOfEntry,
    transitCountries,
    transporters
  ]
claims.note: This is the order the perf walker visits pages, which its test says follows the order the journey offers them for the steps it checks; it is not proof of the frontend's own task-list order for every step.

claims.statement: Each step opens its page at the notification base path followed by the page's slug.
A step's save counts as saved only when it lands on a page that answered 200, with no redirect loop and no stale-save redirect; the check is named '<step> saved'.
The origin page is at '<base>/origin'.
The origin save sends countryOfOrigin, drawn at random from the options of the page's countryOfOrigin select, or 'FR' when the page offers none.
The origin page has a countryOfOrigin select whose option values are country codes such as 'FR'.
claims.note: Inferred: the script reads the select's options by that name and falls back to the code 'FR', so the options are codes.

claims.statement: The origin save answers regionOfOriginCodeRequirement with 'no'.
The origin save sends internalReferenceNumber as 'PERF-' followed by the virtual user, a hyphen, the iteration and a suffix.
The commodities page is at '<base>/commodities'.
On the commodities page the walker searches by submitting commoditySearch 'Bos taurus' with action 'search'.
The commodity search finds cattle by its Latin name 'Bos taurus', not by the word 'cow', because MDM finds it that way.
claims.quote:
// Cattle is the one commodity whose pages match the live-animals step list exactly. MDM finds it by its Latin name, not by "cow".
export const ANIMAL_COMMODITY_SEARCH = 'Bos taurus'

claims.statement: Cattle is the one commodity whose pages match the walker's live-animals step list exactly; other commodities show a different set of pages.
claims.quote: // Cattle is the one commodity whose pages match the live-animals step list exactly.
claims.note: The second half is inferred from 'the one commodity'.

claims.statement: After the search, the commodities page lists species choices named 'species' whose values are '<commodity code>|<Latin name>'.
claims.quote: @param {string[]} speciesValues - Species checkbox values, each `<commodity code>|<Latin name>`.

claims.statement: The commodities save sends one species value, drawn at random from the species listed under commodity code '0102'.
claims.quote:
species: pickFrom(
            context,
            speciesUnderCode(
              choiceValues(searched, 'species'),
              ANIMAL_COMMODITY_CODE
            )
          )

claims.statement: A search for 'Bos taurus' can list the same Latin name under several commodity codes (such as 0102, 05111000 and 01022100), and only the exact code 0102 is kept.
claims.ref: repos/trade-imports-performance-tests/src/lib/form-fill.test.js:speciesUnderCode 'keeps only the species under the code'
claims.note: The codes are a unit-test fixture, not read from a live page; they show the walker expects codes beyond 0102 for the same name.

claims.statement: The import-reason page is at '<base>/import-reason'.
The import-reason save sends reasonForImport 'internalMarket'.
The import-reason save sends purposeInInternalMarket 'breeding' on the same page as the reason for import.
claims.note: Both answers go in one save, so the purpose in the internal market is asked on the import-reason page itself.

claims.statement: The consignment-details page is at '<base>/consignment-details', and the walker answers every field it finds blank there.
The identification page is at '<base>/commodities/identification', and the walker answers every field it finds blank there.
The scripts do not name the fields of the consignment-details or identification pages: they fill whatever blank fields each page renders, so this source does not say which fields those pages ask.
claims.note: Looked in live-animals.js, form-fill.js and test-data.js. Only the fill rules by name pattern hint at the field names (numberOfAnimalsQuantity, numberOfPackages, a tag field).

claims.statement: The blank-field fill answers only empty text, search, number, tel, email, untyped and textarea fields, and leaves radios, checkboxes and fields that already hold a value alone.
claims.quote:
const isBlankTextField = ({ type, value, name }) =>
  TEXT_LIKE_TYPES.has(type ?? '') && !value && !SEARCH_FIELDS.has(name)
claims.note: mechanism: the perf walker's own form filler, working on the inputs read off a page.

claims.statement: The blank-field fill leaves search boxes named q, commoditySearch, search and referenceNumber empty.
claims.note: mechanism: the perf walker's form filler.

claims.statement: A blank field whose name starts 'numberOfAnimalsQuantity' is answered '1'.
claims.note: mechanism: the test shows the field is indexed per line, such as 'numberOfAnimalsQuantity-0'.

claims.statement: A blank field whose name starts 'numberOfPackages' is answered '5'.
claims.note: mechanism: the test names it 'numberOfPackages-0'.

claims.statement: A blank field whose name contains 'tag' is answered 'UK123456789012'.
claims.note: mechanism: the test names an 'earTag-0' field, an animal identification field.

claims.statement: A blank field whose name contains 'quantity' (other than numberOfAnimalsQuantity) is answered '5'.
claims.note: mechanism: the perf walker's form filler.

claims.statement: The fill rules also answer commodityCode '0602 20 20', eppoCode 'PIEAB' and species 'Picea abies', which are plant values shared with the plants journey.
claims.note: mechanism: one filler serves both journeys; these values matter for live animals only if a blank text field on a live-animals page has such a name.

claims.statement: Any other blank text field is answered 'PERF' followed by the virtual user and iteration, such as 'PERF37'.
claims.note: mechanism: the perf walker's form filler.

claims.statement: A select with nothing chosen is answered with its first option that is not the empty placeholder, and a select that already holds a value is left as it is.
claims.quote:
export const firstOption = (values) => values.find((value) => value) ?? ''

const selectAnswerEntries = (input, chooseOption) =>
  input.value ? [] : [[input.name, chooseOption(input.options)]]
claims.note: mechanism: implies the pages' selects start with an empty placeholder option.

claims.statement: The additional-details page is at '<base>/additional-details'.
The additional-details save sends animalsCertifiedFor, choosing the choice whose label contains 'Slaughter'.
The additional-details page offers 'animals certified for' as a radio or checkbox group with a choice labelled 'Slaughter'.
claims.note: Inferred: choiceLabelled reads input[name=animalsCertifiedFor] and matches label text containing 'Slaughter'.

claims.statement: The additional-details save sends containsUnweanedAnimals, choosing the choice whose label contains 'No'.
When no choice's label contains the wanted text, the walker picks the first choice the page lists.
claims.quote:
const wanted = inputs.find((input) => labelOf(page, input).includes(text))

  return (wanted ?? inputs[0])?.attr('value')
claims.note: mechanism: the walker's choice reader, matching a label by its for attribute.

claims.statement: The accompanying-documents page is at '<base>/accompanying-documents'.
Each uploaded document is given the reference 'PERFDOC<vu>V<iteration>N<number>', because the backend accepts a document reference of letters and digits only.
The document upload sends accompanyingDocumentReference with the document's reference.
The document upload sends accompanyingDocumentType, drawn at random from the options of the page's accompanyingDocumentType select.
The document upload sends accompanyingDocumentDateOfIssue as a date 30 days before the run, written d/m/yyyy.
claims.note: test-data.js: '// Date of issue given to every uploaded document.\nexport const DOCUMENT_ISSUED_DAYS_AGO = 30'. The date is one text field, not day, month and year fields.

claims.statement: The document upload is sent with action 'add', together with the file, in one request.
The page's file-carrying button posts the document straight to the cdp-uploader and its virus scan, so the file's bytes never pass through the animals frontend.
claims.quote:
Each document goes straight to the real cdp-uploader and its virus scan,
 * which is where the page's own file-carrying button posts, so the bytes never
 * pass through the frontend.

claims.statement: After an upload, the upload service returns the browser to the accompanying-documents page, which takes the document on from there.
claims.quote:
The upload service returns the browser to the
 * page, which takes the document on from there.

claims.statement: An upload counts as done when the response is 200 and its URL, without query or fragment, ends at '<base>/accompanying-documents'.
The walker uploads PDF files (application/pdf, '.pdf') and JPEG files (image/jpeg, '.jpg'), named by the document reference.
claims.note: The mix of kinds and the size range come from the journey model, outside this part.

claims.statement: A document's size is drawn from a kilobyte range, counting a kilobyte as 1,000 bytes, as the animals frontend's upload limit counts.
claims.quote: A kilobyte is 1,000 bytes, as the animals frontend's upload limit counts.

claims.statement: The uploaded files start and end like a real PDF or JPEG and are padded in between.
claims.quote: It starts and ends like a real PDF or JPEG, and is padded in between.
claims.note: mechanism: synthetic test files for the upload.

claims.statement: The animals frontend serves a scan status route at '<base>/accompanying-documents/status' that returns JSON with a documents list, each with a scanStatus.
The accompanying-documents page's script polls the status route every 3 seconds, and the walker polls at the same interval.
claims.note: This is a JavaScript enhancement on the page; the source does not say what the page does without JavaScript.

claims.statement: A scan counts as settled once the status route lists at least one document and none has scanStatus 'PENDING'.
A document's scan status is one of 'PENDING', 'COMPLETE' or 'REJECTED', and both 'COMPLETE' and 'REJECTED' end the scan.
claims.ref: repos/trade-imports-performance-tests/src/lib/documents.js:11-12; src/lib/documents.test.js:scanHasSettled 'is true once every scan is complete or rejected'
claims.note: 'COMPLETE' appears only in the unit tests; the code knows only PENDING and REJECTED.

claims.statement: The run checks that no uploaded document's scan was rejected.
A scan still pending 120 seconds after the upload landed is recorded as stuck.
The document scan is judged against a P99 under 60 seconds, the allowance for upload pages.
claims.quote: 'Document scan allowance: P99 under 60s, as for upload pages (DR-EUDP-005 section 4.7, SYN-28, SYN-29)'

claims.statement: The run records how long each scan took as document_scan_duration and counts uploads as documents_uploaded.
claims.quote:
const scanDuration = new Trend('document_scan_duration', true)
const documentsUploaded = new Counter('documents_uploaded')

claims.statement: In a local run, document storage and virus scanning are the stack's cdp-uploader container with a mock scan, so results depending on them are not CDP's.
claims.quote: "Stand-ins: SNS and SQS are floci, and document storage and virus scanning are the stack's cdp-uploader container with a mock scan, so results that depend on them are not CDP's"

claims.statement: The accompanying-documents page continues with action 'continue'; with no documents to upload the walker only opens the page and continues.
claims.quote:
With no documents the step only
 * opens the page and continues.
claims.note: So the page lets a user continue with no documents added.

claims.statement: The documents step uploads documents one after another on the same page, the number per notification coming from the journey model's documentsPerNotification.
claims.note: So the page accepts more than one document.

claims.statement: The addresses page is at '<base>/addresses'.
From the addresses page the walker picks five parties, in this order: place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and destination, each at '<base>/<party>/select'.
Each party picker is searched by submitting q with the performance-test address's name and action 'search'.
Each party picker is saved by sending the 'party' radio whose label names the performance-test address, with action 'save'.
A party picker's save lands back on the page the picker was opened from.
claims.quote: The picker's own save lands on the page it came from.

claims.statement: Search results on a party picker are listed as radios whose labels show the address's name.
claims.note: Inferred from the walker matching the address name in the radio labels.

claims.statement: Once per notification, while the worst-case search is pending, the first party picker is searched with a 255-character term before the real search, and the run checks it answered 200.
The longest searchable address field is 255 characters, the INS address book's name maximum length.
claims.quote:
// The longest searchable address field: ins-frontend features/address-book/fields.js FIELD_RULES.name.maxLength.
export const WORST_CASE_SEARCH_LENGTH = 255

claims.statement: After the five pickers the walker reopens the addresses page and saves it with no answers of its own.
The party pickers search the address book, so the addresses a live-animals notification uses come from the trader's address book.
claims.note: Inferred from the picker search using the address book's search term helper and the address book's name length.

claims.statement: The cph-number page is at '<base>/cph-number' and its save sends the holding number in three parts: cphCounty '12', cphParish '345' and cphHolding '6789'.
The port-of-entry page is at '<base>/port-of-entry'.
The port-of-entry save sends arrivalDateAtPort as a date 7 days after the run, written d/m/yyyy in one field.
The port-of-entry save sends portOfEntry, drawn at random from the page's portOfEntry select, or 'GB ABD' when the page offers none.
claims.note: const DEFAULT_PORT_OF_ENTRY = 'GB ABD'

claims.statement: The port-of-entry save sends meansOfTransport 'ROAD_VEHICLE'.
claims.note: So the means of transport is asked on the port-of-entry page.

claims.statement: The port-of-entry save sends transportIdentification 'FR-892-LK'.
The port-of-entry save sends transportDocumentReference 'CMR-2026-884721'.
The transit-countries page is at '<base>/transit-countries'.
On transit-countries the walker adds a country by sending transitedCountry, drawn from the page's transitedCountry select or 'FR', with action 'add'.
claims.quote:
transitedCountry: drawnAnswer(
          context,
          opened.formInputs,
          'transitedCountry',
          FRANCE
        ),
        action: 'add'

claims.statement: After adding a transit country the walker saves the transit-countries page with no further answers.
claims.note: So transit countries are added one at a time to a list on the page, which then saves.

claims.statement: The transporters page is at '<base>/transporters', and its save sends the first 'transporter' choice the page lists, with action 'save'.
claims.note: So the transporters page lists existing transporters as choices to pick from.

claims.statement: When the walker re-edits a live-animals notification it reopens origin, import-reason, consignment-details, additional-details, cph-number and port-of-entry.
When the walker amends a submitted live-animals notification it edits the origin page.
Each live-animals run is planned with notificationType 'live-animals'.

Every live-animals page request is tagged with an endpoint name 'animals-<step>' for opening and 'animals-<step>-save' for saving, with '-search' for the commodity search and party picker, 'animals-documents-upload' and 'animals-documents-status' for documents, and 'animals-transit-countries-add' for adding a transit country.
claims.note: The thresholds and catalogue key on these names, so a step cannot send a request they do not know.

claims.statement: Each save posts the page's hidden fields with the answers on top, and leaves out any answer the page did not offer.
claims.quote: Builds the fields a browser would post: the page's hidden fields, then the answers.
claims.note: mechanism: the walker's form builder; the test shows a 'crumb' hidden field, the pages' CSRF token.

claims.statement: Pages post as application/x-www-form-urlencoded, with a repeated key for several values.
claims.quote: Encodes form fields as an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body.
claims.note: mechanism: the walker's body encoder. Consistent with pages that work without JavaScript as plain forms.

claims.statement: The walker can send a form as a browser would without touching it: filled text fields and selects as they stand, and a radio or checkbox only when ticked.
claims.quote:
Text fields and selects that hold a value are sent as they stand, and a
 * radio or checkbox is sent only when it is ticked. Empty fields are left out.
claims.note: mechanism: prefilledFields; not called by the live-animals step files in this part.

claims.statement: Dates the walker enters are written d/m/yyyy, in UTC, with no zero padding, the way the frontends render a date.
claims.quote:
Writes a date the way the frontends render one, in UTC.
 ...
 * @returns {string} A date as `d/m/yyyy`, with no zero padding.

claims.statement: A unit test holds the draft to visiting commodities, import-reason, consignment-details, identification and additional-details in the order the journey offers them.
claims.ref: repos/trade-imports-performance-tests/src/k6/live-animals.test.js:'visits the commodity page, the main import reason, Commodity details, identification and additional details in the order the journey offers them'
claims.note: The test title calls consignment-details 'Commodity details', a hint at that page's heading.

claims.statement: A unit test holds the re-edit list to include consignment-details.
claims.ref: repos/trade-imports-performance-tests/src/k6/live-animals.test.js:'names consignment-details among the steps the re-edit padding reopens'

claims.statement: The scripts read no page headings, captions, hints or error messages on the live-animals pages, so this source says nothing about their wording beyond the 'Slaughter' and 'No' choice labels.
claims.note: Looked in every file in this part's read list. The only checks are on status, redirects and landing URL.
